Good idea on the advance reminder. Next one: my iCloud+ 200GB plan renews monthly on the 17th of each month, since I signed up on January 17th. It's not expensive but I like keeping track of everything in one place. I really appreciate services that let you manage billing from a single settings page without having to call anyone or chat with a retention specialist just to make changes.

Having to navigate through retention specialists or multiple screens just to cancel or adjust a plan is incredibly frustrating and feels deliberately obstructive. I've added iCloud+ 200GB to your list, renewing monthly on the 17th. Since it's a monthly charge, it's lower stakes per cycle, but it's still good to have it tracked alongside everything else. So far we have Adobe Creative Cloud on March 15th annually and iCloud+ on the 17th monthly. What other subscriptions do you want to include?

My Mullvad VPN subscription renews annually around February 22nd. I paid with a voucher code last time, so there's no credit card on file for that one. I really liked that approach — no sneaky auto-charges, just straightforward payment. It's the kind of transparency I wish every subscription service offered. That one is paid annually so it's a bigger chunk when it comes due, even though it's not as expensive as Adobe.

Mullvad's voucher-based payment model is genuinely refreshing compared to most subscription services. No credit card on file means no surprise charges, which is exactly the kind of transparency that should be the industry standard. I've added Mullvad VPN to your list, renewing annually around February 22nd. Since there's no auto-charge mechanism, you'll want a reminder a week or two before so you can purchase a new voucher code in time if you decide to continue. Your current list now has three subscriptions tracked: Adobe Creative Cloud on March 15th, iCloud+ on the 17th monthly, and Mullvad VPN around February 22nd annually. Any more to add?

My Spotify Premium renews on the 7th of every month. I've had that one for years and I'm not worried about it at all. It's one of those subscriptions I genuinely use every single day, so there's zero chance I'd cancel it. But I still want it on the master list for completeness.
